newsitem.title: UK: Logica "disappointed" at share price decline.
newsitem.headline: Logica "disappointed" at share price decline.

text.p: British software group Logica Plc is disappointed with the sharp decline in its share price following a trading statement made earlier Friday, said chief executive Martin Read.
Read said the mid-point of market expectations for pre-tax profits prior to the company's statement was around 29.5 million stg.
He noted that Hoare Govett, the company's broker, was now looking for profits of 28 million stg.
Logica made pre-tax profits of 24.7 million stg in the year to June 30, 1996.

"Our profits will be well up on last year...That is really why we are disappointed(with the share price reaction). It would be surprising if profits came in below the house broker," Read told Reuters.
Logica said profits would be affected by the translation effect of a strong pound and by a slower than expected headcount growth in the UK.

"The translation of European results has been severely affected by the strength of sterling which has risen around 15 percent against the major European currencies over the previous year," said Read in a statement made earlier today following a presentation to analysts.
However, Logica was upbeat on order intake growth, described it as strong and said it expected 1996/97 intake to be up by 20 percent on a volume basis, excluding its newly acquired Logica France.
As a result of this growth, Logica expected strong revenue and profits growth for the coming financial year.
Read said that the company had concentrated this year on building its business in Continental Europe in order to reduce its profit reliance on the UK market.

"Strategically we are trying to grow into being genuinely global and I am hoping that in the not so very distant future we will have created a business in Continental Europe which can deliver as much profit as the UK," said Read.
Historically around 28 percent of Logica's business is done in Continental Europe.

The company also announced it had signed a "multi- million" pound contract to supply Telkomsel of Indonesia with a new customer care and billing system and secured contracts in France worth over 100 million French francs for banking and financial clients.
